extracted.intended_audience: ARIPO patent examiners; patent applicants and patent practitioners filing/ prosecuting ARIPO applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for substantive examination and preparation of ARIPO patent applications, covering abstracts, description, drawings, biological deposits, claims form/content, and transmittal/search-report procedures. Intended to guide examiners and inform applicants on required content and examination practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies for reviews or books cited
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a review or a book, copies should be made of the title page and the relevant pages of the publication concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling summaries, extracts or abstracts cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a document cited is a summary, extract or abstract of another document published separately, a copy of the summary, extract or abstract is forwarded to the applicant; if the Search Examiner considers the entire document is required, that document must be cited and a copy attached to the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For references obtained by online search where neither the printed database version nor original article is available at the ARIPO Office when drafting the search report, the print-out is added to the file in lieu of the original. A database print-out may substitute for the printed abstract if there is no difference in relevant technical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of search report and opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARIPO Office forwards the search report, the search opinion (if applicable) and copies of all cited documents to the applicant, including those documents appearing after the '&' sign and designated to be copied and sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must contain an abstract to give brief technical information about the disclosure as contained in the description, claims and any drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner determines definitive abstract content
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is initially supplied by the applicant; the examiner determines its definitive content (normally published with the application) and should consider the abstract in relation to the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract is for technical information only and must not be used to interpret the scope of protection sought. Draft the abstract to be an efficient searching instrument and to allow assessment of whether the full application should be consulted. If the search report is published later than the application, the abstract resulting from examination will be the published one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements of the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must (i) indicate the title of the invention; (ii) indicate the technical field to which the invention pertains; (iii) contain a concise summary of the disclosure sufficient to understand the technical problem, gist of the solution and principal use (include characteristic chemical formula where applicable); (iv) not contain statements on alleged merits or speculative applications; (v) preferably not contain more than 150 words; (vi) be accompanied by an indication of the figure (or exceptionally figures) of the drawings to accompany the abstract, with reference signs in parentheses after each main feature mentioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure selection accompanying abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should consider selection of figures to publish with the abstract and may alter the abstract text accordingly; the examiner may select different figures or prevent publication of any drawing with the abstract if none are useful for understanding the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate on conciseness and clarity; refrain from altering language merely for embellishment. If the applicant requested particular drawings, the examiner may still withhold them if not useful for understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use WIPO ST.12 checklist for abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering the abstract, the examiner should check it against the General Guidelines for the Preparation of Abstracts of Patent Documents, using the checklist contained in WIPO Standard ST.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of abstract to applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the abstract is transmitted to the applicant together with the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examiner considers search opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed with a search opinion, the Examining Section will consider both the objections raised in the search opinion and the applicant's response when examining the application further; the position may change after arguments, amendments, top-up searches, or further prior art brought to attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of examination report for PCT-derived applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application derives from an International (PCT) application and is subject to a supplementary ARIPO search, the examination report is based on the application documents constituting the latest filed request from the applicant; supplementary search reports are also based on these documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may involve cancellation of previously filed amendments and reversion in part or full to an earlier set of application documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an ARIPO application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must contain: (i) a request; (ii) a description; (iii) one or more claims; (iv) one or more drawings (where required); (v) an abstract; (vi) a designation of the Contracting State for which a patent is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter discusses items (ii) description and (iv) drawings insofar as they concern substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract has no legal effect on scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract relates to the application as filed and published; its final form for publication is determined by the Examination Division, but it is not necessary to bring it into conformity with the content of the published patent; the abstract has no legal effect and cannot be used to interpret the scope of protection or to justify adding new subject-matter to the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may seek amendment of the abstract but must note its non-legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title should clearly and concisely state the technical designation of the invention and should exclude all fancy names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While formalities examination may catch obvious failures, the substantive examiner should review the title in light of the description and claims and ensure it gives a clear and adequate indication of the subject of the invention; if claim categories change, check whether the title needs corresponding amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure in the description (Rule 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARIPO application must disclose the invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purposes: ensure technical information to enable practice of the invention and enable the reader to understand the inventor's contribution to the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended description subheadings
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should start with the same title as in the request and contain subheadings corresponding to: 'Technical Field', 'Background Art', 'Disclosure of Invention', 'Brief Description of Drawings', 'Best Mode(s) for Carrying Out the Invention', 'Industrial Applicability', and, where appropriate, 'Sequence Listing' and 'Sequence Listing Free Text'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of such subheadings is strongly recommended to provide uniformity and facilitate access to information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical field statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The application should specify the technical field to which it relates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background art disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should mention any background art of which the applicant is aware and which is useful for understanding the invention and its relationship to the prior art; identification of documents, especially patent specifications, should preferably be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly apply to background art corresponding to technical features necessary for definition of the claimed subject matter but which, in combination, are part of the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of the invention (problem and solution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention as claimed should be disclosed so that the technical problem(s) can be appreciated and the solution understood; include only details necessary for elucidating the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not necessary to present explicitly in problem-and-solution form. State advantageous effects but do not disparage prior art or present ambiguous comparisons that mislead about prior art accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings are included they should first be briefly described (e.g., 'Figure 1 is a plan view...'); when referring to elements, name the element as well as its number (e.g., 'resistor 3 is connected to capacitor 5 via switch 4').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description and drawings should be consistent in reference numbers and signs. Examiner need not rigorously require deletion of superfluous drawing references after certain amendments, but references used in description or claims should also appear on drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The ARIPO application should set forth at least the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the invention, indicated in terms of examples and with reference to drawings where appropriate; applicant should point out which embodiments they consider the best mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance requires two inquiries: (1) subjective—did applicant contemplate a best mode at filing; (2) objective—was it disclosed sufficiently for a skilled person to practice it. Examiner should assume best mode is disclosed unless inconsistent evidence. Practices diverge among authorities; some designated States do not require best mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe both structure and function
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention should be described in terms of its structure and also in terms of its function, unless functions are immediately apparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In some fields (e.g., computers) clear functional description may be more appropriate than over-detailed structural description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure and irreparable insufficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must supply sufficient disclosure to meet Rule 6 for all claims; where disclosure is insufficient to enable a skilled person to carry out the claimed invention, claims may be too broad and unsupported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two special instances of fundamental insufficiency: (a) success dependent on chance (results not reproducible, e.g., certain microbiological mutation processes); (b) inherently impossible performance contrary to established physical laws (e.g., perpetual motion machine). Distinguish from processes with some failure rate that can be sorted by nondestructive testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide/amino acid sequence listing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application contains nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences, the description should contain a separate sequence listing part, which may be in written and computer-readable form or filed on an electronic medium if the receiving Office accepts electronic submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of biological material for sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application refers to biological material that cannot otherwise be described to meet Rule 6, a deposit of such material is taken into consideration when determining whether sufficiency requirements are met; deposit is considered part of the description to that extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere reference to deposited material may not replace explicit disclosure. In some Authorities deposit is also considered for the support requirement of claims (Rule 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation for deposited microorganisms/biological material
rubrics_metrics.description: The manner and order of presentation of description parts should follow Rule 6(1) unless a different arrangement better aids understanding; examiner should exercise discretion about objections to presentation—some departure acceptable if description is clear and orderly and information is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements of Rule 6(1) may be waived for fortuitous discoveries, inventions breaking new ground, or certain technically simple inventions comprehensible with minimal description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and definition of technical terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The description should be clear and straightforward, avoiding unnecessary technical jargon; generally accepted technical terms, signs and symbols should be used; little-known or specially formulated terms may be allowed if adequately defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency of terminology is important. Foreign terms allowed when no equivalent in ARIPO application language. Established terms must not be used with different meanings. Terms may be borrowed from analogous arts where legitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer-program related disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Program listings in programming languages cannot be relied on as the sole disclosure for computer-related inventions; the description should be written substantially in normal language, possibly with flow diagrams or other aids; short excerpts from programs may illustrate an embodiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units, symbols and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: When properties of a material are referred to, relevant units should be specified; metric system should be used or supplemented with metric equivalents; temperature in degrees Celsius or also in degrees Celsius if different units used; other physical values should use internationally recognized units (e.g., MKSA/SI for electrical units); chemical and mathematical symbols and molecular formulae should be those in general use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reference is made to a published standard, identify it adequately. Adopt agreed international standards in the art where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of proper names and trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of proper names to refer to materials or articles is undesirable where such words denote origin or a range of products; if used, the product should be sufficiently identified to enable carrying out the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception when such words have become internationally accepted standard descriptive terms with precise meaning (e.g., 'Bowden' cable).

rubrics_metrics.name: References to other documents as disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: References to other documents may relate to background art or to part of the disclosure; where the reference relates directly to the disclosure it must be in the application as originally filed and clearly identify the document so it can be retrieved, otherwise it cannot be taken into account for Rule 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If matter in the referred document is essential to satisfy Rule 6, that matter should be incorporated into the description because the patent specification should be self-contained regarding essential features. References to unpublished previously filed applications are not regarded as part of the disclosure unless made public on or before the publication date; references to textbooks/periodicals are allowable only if content fixed prior to international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements and text on drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal requirements for drawings are set in Rule 6(1)(e); the issue is whether text matter on drawings is indispensable. In circuit diagrams and flow sheets, identifying catchwords for functional integers may be indispensable if necessary for rapid interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such items can often be identified by a numeral or letter and explained in the description. Examiner should consider whether text on drawings is absolutely indispensable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments should preferably be identified using editor functions to indicate deletions and insertions; pages with such indications should be submitted in addition to clean copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, hand-written mark-up pages may be submitted provided that clean copies are free from handwritten amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressions not to be used in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Four categories of expressions should not be contained in an ARIPO application: (1) matter contrary to morality or public order (ordre public) such as incitement to riot, incitement to criminal acts, discriminatory propaganda, grossly obscene matter; (2) similar prohibited matter; (3) libelous or disparaging statements (not allowed); and (4) irrelevant matter which is obviously irrelevant or unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to prohibit matter likely to induce riot, crime, or offensive behaviour. Examiner likely to invoke this provision only in rare cases. Distinguish fair comment (permitted) from libelous disparagement (not permitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of irrelevant matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Irrelevant matter that is 'obviously irrelevant or unnecessary' (having no bearing on the subject matter or its background) is prohibited and may need removal; matter may become irrelevant during examination due to claim limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's attention is drawn to PCT Rule 9 for application of these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: general requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims must: (i) define the matter for which protection is sought; (ii) be clear and concise; and (iii) be fully supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This chapter sets out appropriate form and content of claims and how they should be interpreted for assessing novelty, inventive step, and for searching relevant prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims drafted in terms of technical features
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must be drafted in terms of the 'technical features of the invention' and should not contain statements relating to commercial advantages or non-technical matters; statements of purpose are allowed if they assist in defining the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functional limitations are permissible provided a skilled person would have no difficulty in providing means to perform the function without inventive skill or such means are fully disclosed. Evaluate functional limitations in context for what they fairly convey to a skilled person. Claims to the use of the invention (technical application) are permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-part claim (Rules 7(1)(a) and (b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, a claim should take a two-part form: first part indicating designation of subject matter and prior-art features necessary for definition; second 'characterizing portion' stating the technical features which, in combination with first-part features, it is desired to protect (the features the invention adds to the prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invite applicant to use two-part form when invention is a distinct improvement on known combination. Two-part form need only be used when appropriate; inappropriate in cases like (i) combination of known elements of equal status where inventive step is in the combination, (ii) modification of a known chemical process (omitting or substituting substance), (iii) complex systems with interrelated parts. Purpose is to show which features are part of the prior art; if prior-art indication in description makes this clear, alternative claim forms may be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims may contain formulae and tables but not drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims, like the description, may contain chemical or mathematical formulae but not drawings; any claim may contain tables only if the subject matter of the claim makes the use of tables desirable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given the word 'desirable', examiner should not object to tables where convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must not rely on references to description/drawings except absolutely necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must not, in respect of technical features, rely on references to the description or drawings except where absolutely necessary (Rule 7(2)); examples of exceptions include peculiar shapes illustrated in drawings that cannot be readily defined in words or chemical products definable only by graphs or diagrams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should be invited to show that reliance on such references is 'absolutely necessary'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reference signs in claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If drawings are present and technical features of the claims would be rendered more intelligible by relating them to corresponding features of the drawings, appropriate reference signs may be placed in parentheses after features in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference signs are aids to understanding and are not to be construed as limiting the scope of a claim.
